abstract: The Informedia Digital Video Library project is implementing full content search and retrieval from digital video, audio, and text libraries through the utilization of integrated speech, image, and language understanding technologies for automated creation and exploration. Image processing analyzes scenes, speech processing transcribes the audio signal, and natural language processing determines word relevance. Together, these generate a meaningful index into the video content. Segment breaks produced by image processing are examined, along with the boundaries identified by the natural language processing of the transcript to partition the video library into sets of segments, or “video paragraphs.” Automating these techniques into a unified collaborative system uniquely enables us to include and search through vast amounts of video data in the library with little to no human intervention.

authors.bio: Howard D. Wactlar is the viceprovost for research computing and associate dean of the School of Computer Science at Carnegie Mellon University. He was a founder of the Software Engineering Institute and director of the Information Technology Center, a research department focused on large-scale deployment and technology transfer. He was the primary architect and is currently the project director of the Informedia Digital Video Library. His research interests are multimedia, distributed systems, networking, and performance measurement.
authors.name: H. D. Wactlar

authors.bio: Alex Hauptmann is a systems scientist in the Computer Science Dept. at Carnegie Mellon University. He received his B.A. and M.A. degrees in psychology from Johns Hopkins University, studied computer science at Technische Universitaet Berlin from 1982 to 1984, and received his Ph.D. in computer science from Carnegie Mellon in 1991. His research interests have led him to pursue and combine several different areas: man-machine communication, natural language processing, speech understanding, and synthesis. He worked on speech and machine translation at CMU from 1984 to 1997, when he joined the Informedia project where he is researching a news-on-demand application.
authors.name: A. G. Hauptmann

authors.bio: Michael Smith is a doctoral candidate in the Electrical and Computer Engineering Dept. at Carnegie Mellon University. He received his B.S. in electrical engineering from North Carolina A&T State University in 1991 and his M.S.E.E. from Stanford University in 1992. His a member of IEEE as well as Eta Kappa Nu, Tau Beta Pi, and Pi Mu Epsilon. — Smith has published papers on the subjects of pattern recognition, biomedical imaging, video characterization, and interactive computer systems. His current interests are image classification and recognition and content-based image understanding. His research is an active component of the Informedia Digital Video Library project at Carnegie.
authors.name: M. A. Smith

authors.bio: Krishna Pendyala is an information designer with extensive experience in the development of informational and learning applications. He serves as the assistant director of the NSF-sponsored Informedia Digital Video Library project at CMU's School of Computer Science. His research focus is on tools and methodologies for digital, nonlinear networked learning environments. — Pendyala is also the founder of Visual Symphony, Inc., a multimedia software developer that specializes in interactive networked applications to enhance human performance. He serves as a Unesco consultant to India on multimedia infrastructure and development. He is the vice-president of the International Interactive Communications Society (IICS) and the founder of the Pittsburgh Chapter, and a member of the board of directors of the Multimedia Foundry of Pittsburgh, established to promote that city as a center for new media. — Pendyala holds a Master's degree in educational media from Indiana State University and a Bachelor's degree in engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology, Madras, India.
authors.name: K. V. Pendyala

authors.affiliation: ISLIP Media Network, Inc., Pittsburgh, PA 15213.
authors.bio: Dennis Garlington is a founder and principal in the firm of Dalby Emprise, a consultancy which investigates, reports, and advises on the technologies and business motivations creating the convergence of telephones, computers, and video displays. Garlington is a 25-year veteran of the telecommunications and interactive technology industries; he has held executive positions with GTE Interactive Media, Prodigy Services, Times Mirror, Cox Communications, and Memorex Corp.
authors.name: D. Garlington
